title: Sums agree under a compatible relabelling
statement:
Let $f\colon A \to \bbn$ and $g\colon B \to \bbn$ be functions into the natural numbers, let $h\colon A \to B$ be a map, and let $c_1,\dots,c_m$ be a finite list of elements of $A$. If $g(h(c)) = f(c)$ for every entry $c$ of the list, then
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{m} g\bigl(h(c_i)\bigr) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{m} f(c_i),
\]
where each sum is taken over the list in order with initial value $0$.
hypotheses_covered: g(h c) = f c for every element c of the list cs
cs is a finite list over the domain of f and h
replaced:
A technical lemma: if $g(h\,c) = f\,c$ for all $c \in cs$, then the additive
\texttt{foldr} of $g$ over $cs.\mathrm{map}\;h$ equals the additive \texttt{foldr} of $f$
over $cs$.
